primary_invariant: Restore must be deterministic and physical payload metadata must resolve to valid bytes.
secondary_invariants: Store/reclaim/rebuild must not reuse stale physical metadata; packed and legacy read paths must resolve equivalent payload bytes; restore must not escape destination roots.
initial_threshold_direction: baseline required; warn below target; block only on regression without rationale
notes: Highest priority package. Includes store, restore, reclaim, packed/legacy metadata, physical payload reads, and path safety.

primary_invariant: Verify must fail closed on corrupted or inconsistent catalog/storage state.
secondary_invariants: Payload hash mismatch must be detected; packed refs must be checked; legacy blocks must be checked; mixed repositories must be verified consistently.
initial_threshold_direction: baseline required; warn below target; block only on regression without rationale
notes: Critical because false verification success is an S0-style trust failure.

primary_invariant: Maintenance must not delete reachable data or legitimize corrupt mappings.
secondary_invariants: GC orchestration must preserve roots; repair must not turn bad mappings into accepted truth; stats must not hide packed/legacy state inconsistencies.
initial_threshold_direction: baseline required; warn below target; block only on regression without rationale
notes: Covers high-level GC/repair/stats behavior that protects repository correctness.

primary_invariant: GC must never delete snapshot-reachable or current-live data.
secondary_invariants: Reachability roots must include snapshots, pins, current logical files, packed refs, and storage blocks; dry-run/live plans must agree.
initial_threshold_direction: baseline required; warn below target; block only on regression without rationale

primary_invariant: Snapshots must remain immutable roots for restore and retention.
secondary_invariants: Snapshot create/list/delete/restore must preserve graph semantics; snapshot deletion must not remove retained data; lineage behavior must remain deterministic.
initial_threshold_direction: baseline required; warn below target; block only on regression without rationale
notes: Critical because snapshots define retention and restore roots.

primary_invariant: Recovery must fail closed and must not legitimize corrupt mappings.
secondary_invariants: Interrupted operations must become safe states; orphan/missing/corrupt containers must be quarantined or reported; recovery must not silently trust invalid metadata.
initial_threshold_direction: baseline required; warn below target; block only on regression without rationale
notes: Critical because recovery decides whether ambiguous state becomes accepted state.

primary_invariant: Schema bootstrap and migration must preserve catalog semantics across supported backends.
secondary_invariants: SQLite and PostgreSQL behavior must remain compatible; migrations must not lose graph/state information; schema capability detection must be deterministic.
initial_threshold_direction: baseline required; warn below target; block only on regression without rationale
notes: Tier 2 but release-blocking because catalog drift can corrupt higher-level invariants.

primary_invariant: Catalog graph traversal must preserve reachability semantics.
secondary_invariants: Traversal must visit the correct roots once; graph-derived plans must match snapshot/GC/stat/inspect expectations.
initial_threshold_direction: baseline required; warn below target; block only on regression without rationale
notes: Supports GC and snapshot safety; regressions can become deletion or retention bugs.

primary_invariant: Packed and legacy block abstractions must remain semantically aligned.
secondary_invariants: Block metadata must match payload spans; packed offsets/lengths must remain bounded; payload identity must be stable.
initial_threshold_direction: baseline required; warn below target; block only on regression without rationale
notes: Important because packed storage correctness depends on block metadata.

primary_invariant: Container reads and writes must preserve payload integrity and placement bounds.
secondary_invariants: Header validation must reject invalid containers; append operations must record correct offsets and sizes; encrypted/compressed payload accounting must remain consistent.
initial_threshold_direction: baseline required; warn below target; block only on regression without rationale
notes: Important because container placement bugs propagate into restore and verify failures.

primary_invariant: Retention policies must preserve required snapshots and roots.
secondary_invariants: Policy evaluation must be deterministic; delete candidates must not include retained roots; retention preview and live behavior must remain aligned.
initial_threshold_direction: baseline required; warn below target; block only on regression without rationale
notes: Important because retention feeds snapshot deletion and later GC eligibility.

primary_invariant: CLI and JSON contracts must remain stable where automation depends on them.
secondary_invariants: Command parsing must reject dangerous ambiguity; JSON mode must stay machine-consumable; help/usage must not contradict behavior.
notes: Do not turn v1.10.7 into a CLI cleanup release. Track but do not gate globally.

primary_invariant: Stats and inspect must reflect true repository state without mutation.
secondary_invariants: Packed/legacy stats should remain aligned; inspect should not hide graph inconsistencies; observability must not mutate catalog state.
notes: Important visibility package, but not a first hard-gate target.

primary_invariant: Benchmark reports must be deterministic and schema-valid.
secondary_invariants: Benchmark comparison should not silently accept malformed rows; outputs should avoid NaN/Infinity artifacts.
notes: Avoid mixing benchmark cleanup into v1.10.7 unless coverage tooling directly depends on it.

primary_invariant: Release helper scripts must produce valid artifacts and fail clearly.
secondary_invariants: Generated JSON/CSV artifacts should be schema-valid; malformed inputs should fail closed where used by release gates.
notes: Only observe in v1.10.7 unless a script is introduced or modified for coverage reporting.

primary_invariant: Adversarial tests must keep protecting correctness-critical behavior without becoming product logic.
secondary_invariants: Long-run and race validation should expose storage, GC, restore, recovery, and snapshot regressions.
initial_threshold_direction: report only; no package coverage gate
notes: Test package coverage itself is not the target; its existence is evidence for invariants.

primary_invariant: Integration tests must preserve cross-package behavior and compatibility evidence.
secondary_invariants: SQLite/PostgreSQL, codec, migration, restore, and workflow coverage should remain visible.
initial_threshold_direction: report only; no package coverage gate
notes: Do not gate test package coverage directly.
